key_insight: The paper argues that interpretability can be used before post-training to identify which latent concepts a preference dataset teaches, so teams can shape learning signals at the concept level instead of optimizing opaque scalar rewards.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners building aligned language models, this offers a workflow to audit preference data, reduce off-target behaviors like sycophancy or over-stylization, and intentionally amplify desired traits such as safeguards or persona.
method: Use interpretability protocols to infer latent concepts that separate preferred from dispreferred generations.
Turn those concepts into explicit hypotheses for fine-grained user feedback and dataset inspection.
Unify feature or data interventions as ways to shape rewards during post-training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical results showing the pipeline can diagnose undesirable signals in existing preference data, mitigate off-target learning, and help shape desired properties like safeguards and model personality.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable interpretability signals and careful concept identification, so misleading probes or weak annotations could cause the wrong behaviors to be amplified.
paper_title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
